title: AFTER UPDATE Trigger — Log Salary Changes
description: Create a trigger to log salary changes into an audit table whenever an employee's salary is updated.

data.text: Write an AFTER UPDATE trigger on the `Employees` table that logs salary changes (old and new values) into a `SalaryAudit` table whenever the `Salary` column is modified.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- First, create the audit table
CREATE TABLE SalaryAudit (
    AuditID INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    EmployeeID INT,
    OldSalary DECIMAL(10,2),
    NewSalary DECIMAL(10,2),
    ChangedAt DATETIME DEFAULT GETDATE(),
    ChangedBy NVARCHAR(128) DEFAULT SUSER_SNAME()
);

-- Then, create the trigger
CREATE TRIGGER trg_AfterSalaryUpdate
ON Employees
AFTER UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    INSERT INTO SalaryAudit (EmployeeID, OldSalary, NewSalary)
    SELECT
        d.EmployeeID,
        d.Salary AS OldSalary,
        i.Salary AS NewSalary
    FROM deleted d
    INNER JOIN inserted i ON d.EmployeeID = i.EmployeeID
    WHERE d.Salary <> i.Salary OR (d.Salary IS NULL AND i.Salary IS NOT NULL)
       OR (d.Salary IS NOT NULL AND i.Salary IS NULL);
END;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: AFTER triggers fire after the DML operation completes. The `deleted` pseudo-table holds old row values; `inserted` holds new values. Always check for actual changes (<> or IS NULL logic) to avoid logging no-op updates. Triggers operate in batches — use set-based logic, not cursors.
